name: Windsurf (now Devin Desktop)
tagline: The agentic IDE that was Codeium, then Windsurf, now Cognition’s Devin Desktop, a command centre for coding agents.
verdict: Windsurf was one of the best agentic IDEs of its generation, and as Devin Desktop it is now something more ambitious: a vendor-neutral command centre where local and cloud agents — Cognition’s own plus Claude Agent and Codex via the open ACP — run inside one polished editor (Gemini CLI could too, but Google restricted free access to it in June 2026, and its Antigravity CLI replacement isn’t ACP-compatible yet). That openness is a real differentiator in a field of walled-garden tools, and the shared free/$20 subscription with Devin makes it easy to try. The cost is turbulence: Codeium became Windsurf, Windsurf became Devin Desktop, and the original Cascade agent was switched off on 1 July 2026 — a lot of change for a tool teams use daily. Its default SWE models are also a notch behind frontier models on the hardest tasks, though you can route to those. Pick it if you want an open, multi-agent desktop IDE and are comfortable inside Cognition’s ecosystem; skip it if you want a lightweight editor extension or you specifically wanted the standalone Windsurf that no longer exists.
